Three read-only audits on 2026-11-24 (reports committed on branch `docs/review-checklist` under `docs/audits/2026-11-24-*.md`) found that our recurring review findings are one root problem in three places: a DECISION is made from something that is not evidence. Extractor: a spelling (PascalCase callee, name lists, `contains("Component")`) or a raw expression. Wire boundary (crates/semantic): an ABSENT or defaulted field read as a value (`#[serde(default)]`, `unwrap_or(false)`, tsrs omits empty fields). Caches and sessions: a DEGRADED result (timeout, read failure, heap budget, nesting cut) stored as authoritative. The rules already exist in prose (CONTRIBUTING 'Before you push', ADR 0025-0028: by binding not spelling, one owner per decision, unknown unless proven, always emit a Diagnostic when degrading); nothing enforces them in code.

**Why:** reviews found 3 + 3 + 5 findings per PR in the same classes; each fix moved the problem (validating on a shared cache primed it the other way). Fixing per site does not converge.

**How to apply (direction, in this order):** (1) failing-first counter-example suites (extractor M10: every snippet in the audit becomes a row asserting exact output); (2) make invalid states unrepresentable: `ComponentEvidence` required to build a `ComponentMapping`, a typed `Peeled` (Transparent | Instantiated | Asserted) with one exhaustive match, `Known<T>` for decoded wire fields, a `Degraded` marker on outcomes that no cache or kept answer stores, `CallError::Contract` for undecodable responses with its own code; (3) one owner modules (`extractor/decide.rs`, `semantic/src/wire.rs` with one tsrs version-pin test, one `Memo` abstraction); (4) architecture tests (grep-based Rust tests, no new scripts) that fail on a catch-all arm or a name literal in a decision, `unwrap_or(false)` on wire values, text matching of messages, statics in non-test code; (5) determinism as a tested property: differential tests with separate state per consumer as oracle, session equals cold extract under random edit scripts. Amend ADR 0027/0026: 'a name is a candidate filter, never a verdict'. Related: [[diagnose-after-three-findings]], [[workers-run-full-lint-gate]].

On 2026-11-14 the user said they were "disappointed that you're not taking a step back to understand the patterns, consider the architecture and our models" after the Storybook live-upgrade PR (#462) collected 11 findings over 5 rounds that I routed one at a time as spot fixes. I had promised a model-based approach "if another finding appears" and still patched the next one.

**Why:** findings arrive serially from a reviewer that sees a slice each round; workers capped at 25-35 calls patch the symptom. The 11 findings shared four root causes: no explicit lifecycle model (state scattered across flags keyed by the wrong dimension: component instead of component+revision+key+client), decisions made in two places (lazy vs eager, structural vs checker diagnostics, two dev servers), last-writer-wins singletons where truth is a per-client set, and TypeScript re-deriving what the Rust core already owns. Same smell as #455 (two walkers decide eligibility), #459 (two paths feed the kept answer), #458.

**How to apply:**
- Third finding on a PR: stop; make a table of the findings, name the root causes, ask 'is one decision made or held in two places?' and 'what is the state machine and who owns it?'.
- Remedy shape: one owner for each decision (prefer the Rust core's merged answer over re-deriving in TS), one explicit reducer (pure state x event -> state x effects), and a model-based/property test of the invariants after quiescence, with the earlier findings as named regression sequences.
- Give such a worker room (cap ~100 calls, Opus); caps suit mechanical work, not stateful mechanisms.
- Before accepting any worker fix ask: is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?

**Second instance, 2026-11-15 (#467, tsrs_module swapped for oxc_resolver):** five findings in five rounds, each in glue code that re-created an old behaviour (symlink canonicalization, `.cts` conditions, relative tsconfig, fingerprint inputs, a `baseUrl` fallback that guessed which rule answered from whether the path contained `node_modules`). I called the root cause settled twice and was wrong twice. The user: "How are you not guarding against these coming up???"

**Why:** a behaviour-preserving library swap was gated by a single-run identity diff on two fixtures, which cannot see cross-run cache staleness or inputs the fixtures lack; fix rounds added new heuristic code that nothing exercised; the Entire reviewer was the first real review. The swap's premise ("same results, less code") was false: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 (no `baseUrl` for bare specifiers) where the old resolver followed TypeScript 6, and the PR grew to +768/-222.

**How to apply:**
- Before a swap: inventory every behaviour of the replaced component that the code relies on (options, conditions, symlinks, config inheritance, cache keys) and diff old against new over the cross-product, not two fixtures.
- Before pushing any worker branch: read the diff myself for heuristics (a rule inferred from path shape, a guess) and run `/code-review` on it; do not let the Entire reviewer be the first review.
- At the third finding re-test the premise (does the swap still delete more than it adds?), not only the root cause; if not, close the PR.

**Third instance, 2026-11-15 (about 50 findings across trails 404/405):** the user said "consider all of the findings together, architecturally and semantically ... make sure the agents won't find even more things". Eight root classes (silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, contract drift / fields never populated). Table: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md.

**Why:** guards were DENY-lists (enumerate the wrong cases found so far), so each new grammar form (a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) produced the next finding; about 40% of the raw count was the same code repeated in stacked child PRs.

**How to apply:**
- Design guards as ALLOW-lists: a closed set of proven forms, everything else Unknown/Declined; exhaustive matches, no wildcard arms in decisions.
- Run the pre-push gate in worker-contract.md (invariants, grammar sweep with the checker/TS API as oracle, mutation proof, adversarial pass, then /code-review) before any push; generate tests over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Merge stacks in order and retarget children; do not keep a stack alive across review rounds.

See [[resolve-findings-when-fixed]] and [[worker-token-budget]].

15	/// One layer of the wrappers TypeScript erases from a value.
16	enum Wrapper<'b, 'a> {
17	    /// Parentheses, `satisfies` or `!`: the value and its type pass through.
18	    Transparent(&'b Expression<'a>),
19	    /// `as` or `<T>x`: the value passes through, its type is replaced by the one asserted.
20	    Asserted(&'b Expression<'a>, &'b TSType<'a>),

25	/// The wrapper `expr` is, if it is one. The one list of what a wrapper is, and exhaustive so that a new expression kind

93	/// affirmative evidence ([`Evidence::NotRenderable`]); a type the extractor cannot read leaves the call the candidate
94	/// its name makes it ([`Evidence::Unknown`]), as before assertions were read at all.
95	#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
96	pub(super) enum Evidence<'b, 'a> {
97	    /// No assertion, or one that keeps the callee's own type: `typeof` the same expression, `any` and `unknown`. The
98	    /// callee's declaration describes the call.
99	    Identity,
100	    /// A type reference (`(forwardRef as forwardRefType)`). The file may alias it to `typeof` the callee
101	    /// (`SourceDataCollector::describes_call`); otherwise it reads as [`Evidence::Unknown`].
102	    Reference(&'b TSTypeReference<'a>),
103	    /// Every call signature of the asserted type returns what no component is, and at least one what React renders as a

108	    /// `(Object as (v: object) => object)(…)` neither is a component nor renders, whatever its name.

192	/// The type a namespace has, as far as the assertions on it and on the namespaces it is read from say.
193	enum Typed<'b, 'a> {
194	    /// Its own: no assertion, or one that keeps it.
195	    Own,
196	    /// The asserted type, or the type an asserted namespace's type literal declares for the member.

202	fn receiver<'a, 'b>(expr: &'b Expression<'a>) -> Typed<'b, 'a> {
203	    let (expr, _, outermost) = layers(expr);
204	    let declared = match (outermost, expr) {
205	        (Some(ty), _) => Some(ty),
206	        (None, Expression::StaticMemberExpression(object)) => match receiver(&object.object) {

217	        None => Typed::Own,
218	        Some(ty) if matches!(asserted(ty, expr), Evidence::Identity) => Typed::Own,

245	/// Every declaration of `name` among a type literal's members, in order.
246	fn declarations<'a, 'b>(literal: &'b TSTypeLiteral<'a>, name: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = MemberDeclaration<'b, 'a>> {

248	        TSSignature::TSPropertySignature(property) if names_key(&property.key, name) => Some(MemberDeclaration::Typed(

397	/// The evidence of several signatures or declarations of one callee, each read alone: [`Evidence::NotRenderable`] when
398	/// every one is, [`Evidence::NoComponent`] when every one is that or `NotRenderable`, and [`Evidence::Unknown`]
399	/// otherwise or when there are none. One that may give a component keeps the whole callee a candidate.
400	fn combine<'a, 'b>(all: impl Iterator<Item = Evidence<'b, 'a>>) -> Evidence<'b, 'a> {
401	    let mut combined = None;
402	    for evidence in all {
403	        combined = Some(match (combined, evidence) {
404	            (None | Some(Evidence::NotRenderable), Evidence::NotRenderable) => Evidence::NotRenderable,
405	            (None | Some(Evidence::NotRenderable | Evidence::NoComponent), Evidence::NoComponent)
406	            | (Some(Evidence::NoComponent), Evidence::NotRenderable) => Evidence::NoComponent,
407	            (_, Evidence::Identity | Evidence::Reference(_) | Evidence::Unknown)
408	            | (
409	                Some(Evidence::Identity | Evidence::Reference(_) | Evidence::Unknown),
410	                Evidence::NoComponent | Evidence::NotRenderable,
411	            ) => return Evidence::Unknown,
412	        });
413	    }
414	    combined.unwrap_or(Evidence::Unknown)
415	}

417	/// What a call's declared result says about whether it is a component and whether React renders it.
418	#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
419	enum Returns {
420	    /// What React renders as a node and no component is: a string, number, bigint or boolean keyword, `void`, a
421	    /// literal or template literal, a type predicate, an array of those, or a union with one of them and nothing that
422	    /// may be a component.
423	    Node,
424	    /// Neither a component nor a node: the `object`, `symbol` and `never` keywords, an object type with no call or
425	    /// construct signature, an array of those or of `unknown`/`any` (TypeScript does not take `unknown` for a node).
426	    Neither,
427	    /// `null` or `undefined`: what a component may return, and no evidence alone.
428	    Empty,
429	    /// Anything that may be a component or an element, or that the extractor does not read (a reference, `unknown`).
430	    Maybe,
431	}
432	
433	fn result_of(ty: &TSType<'_>) -> Returns {
434	    match ty {
435	        TSType::TSBigIntKeyword(_)
436	        | TSType::TSBooleanKeyword(_)
437	        | TSType::TSNumberKeyword(_)
438	        | TSType::TSStringKeyword(_)
439	        | TSType::TSVoidKeyword(_)
440	        | TSType::TSLiteralType(_)
441	        | TSType::TSTemplateLiteralType(_)
442	        | TSType::TSTypePredicate(_) => Returns::Node,
443	        TSType::TSNeverKeyword(_) | TSType::TSObjectKeyword(_) | TSType::TSSymbolKeyword(_) => Returns::Neither,
444	        TSType::TSNullKeyword(_) | TSType::TSUndefinedKeyword(_) => Returns::Empty,
445	        TSType::TSParenthesizedType(inner) => result_of(&inner.type_annotation),
446	        TSType::TSTypeLiteral(literal) => {
447	            let callable = literal.members.iter().any(|signature| match signature {
448	                TSSignature::TSCallSignatureDeclaration(_) | TSSignature::TSConstructSignatureDeclaration(_) => true,
449	                TSSignature::TSPropertySignature(_)
450	                | TSSignature::TSMethodSignature(_)
451	                | TSSignature::TSIndexSignature(_) => false,
452	            });
453	            if callable { Returns::Maybe } else { Returns::Neither }
454	        }
455	        // `ReactNode[]` and `string[]` render; `unknown[]` does not.
456	        TSType::TSArrayType(array) => match (&array.element_type, result_of(&array.element_type)) {
457	            (TSType::TSAnyKeyword(_) | TSType::TSUnknownKeyword(_), _) => Returns::Neither,
458	            (_, Returns::Maybe) => Returns::Maybe,
459	            (_, Returns::Node | Returns::Empty) => Returns::Node,
460	            (_, Returns::Neither) => Returns::Neither,
461	        },
462	        // The value is one of the members: it may render when one does, and is a candidate when one may be.
463	        TSType::TSUnionType(union) => {
464	            let mut result = Returns::Empty;
465	            for member in &union.types {
466	                result = match (result, result_of(member)) {
467	                    (Returns::Maybe, _) | (_, Returns::Maybe) => return Returns::Maybe,
468	                    (Returns::Node, _) | (_, Returns::Node) => Returns::Node,
469	                    (Returns::Neither, _) | (_, Returns::Neither) => Returns::Neither,
470	                    (Returns::Empty, Returns::Empty) => Returns::Empty,
471	                };
472	            }
473	            result
474	        }
475	        TSType::TSAnyKeyword(_)
476	        | TSType::TSUnknownKeyword(_)
477	        | TSType::TSIntrinsicKeyword(_)
478	        | TSType::TSThisType(_)
479	        | TSType::TSConditionalType(_)
480	        | TSType::TSConstructorType(_)
481	        | TSType::TSFunctionType(_)
482	        | TSType::TSImportType(_)
483	        | TSType::TSIndexedAccessType(_)
484	        | TSType::TSInferType(_)
485	        | TSType::TSIntersectionType(_)
486	        | TSType::TSMappedType(_)
487	        | TSType::TSNamedTupleMember(_)
488	        | TSType::TSTupleType(_)
489	        | TSType::TSTypeOperatorType(_)
490	        | TSType::TSTypeQuery(_)
491	        | TSType::TSTypeReference(_)
492	        | TSType::JSDocNullableType(_)
493	        | TSType::JSDocNonNullableType(_)
494	        | TSType::JSDocUnknownType(_) => Returns::Maybe,
495	    }
496	}

498	/// Whether `typeof name` is the type of `expr`: the same identifier or the same chain of static members, read through
499	/// the namespaces' wrappers (the outermost assertion states the type whatever the namespace was asserted to).
500	fn query_names(name: &TSTypeQueryExprName<'_>, expr: &Expression<'_>) -> bool {
501	    match name {
502	        TSTypeQueryExprName::IdentifierReference(id) => matches!(expr, Expression::Identifier(e) if e.name == id.name),
503	        TSTypeQueryExprName::QualifiedName(qualified) => type_name_names(&qualified.left, &qualified.right, expr),
504	        TSTypeQueryExprName::ThisExpression(_) => matches!(expr, Expression::ThisExpression(_)),
505	        TSTypeQueryExprName::TSImportType(_) => false,
506	    }
507	}

509	fn type_name_names(left: &TSTypeName<'_>, right: &IdentifierName<'_>, expr: &Expression<'_>) -> bool {
510	    let Expression::StaticMemberExpression(member) = expr else { return false };
511	    if member.property.name != right.name {
512	        return false;
513	    }
514	    let object = peel_expr(&member.object);
515	    match left {
516	        TSTypeName::IdentifierReference(id) => matches!(object, Expression::Identifier(e) if e.name == id.name),
517	        TSTypeName::QualifiedName(qualified) => type_name_names(&qualified.left, &qualified.right, object),
518	        TSTypeName::ThisExpression(_) => matches!(object, Expression::ThisExpression(_)),
519	    }
520	}

522	/// Whether a dotted chain (`createButton`, `React.forwardRef`) names `expr`, read through the namespaces' wrappers.
523	fn chain_names(chain: &str, expr: &Expression<'_>) -> bool {
524	    match (chain.rsplit_once('.'), expr) {
525	        (None, Expression::Identifier(id)) => id.name == chain,
526	        (Some((left, right)), Expression::StaticMemberExpression(member)) => {
527	            member.property.name == right && chain_names(left, peel_expr(&member.object))
528	        }
529	        (None | Some(_), _) => false,
530	    }
531	}

591	/// The module-level aliases of a value's type, `type Factory = typeof createButton`, as alias name to the dotted chain
592	/// it queries. Only a name the file declares once in type space is kept: an import, an interface merged with it, a
593	/// type parameter or a namespace's own type of that name may be what a use means, and which one is not read here.
594	pub(super) fn typeof_aliases(program: &Program<'_>) -> FxHashMap<CompactString, CompactString> {
595	    fn chain(name: &TSTypeName<'_>) -> Option<String> {
596	        match name {
597	            TSTypeName::IdentifierReference(id) => Some(id.name.as_str().to_owned()),
598	            TSTypeName::QualifiedName(qualified) => {
599	                Some(format!("{}.{}", chain(&qualified.left)?, qualified.right.name))
600	            }
601	            TSTypeName::ThisExpression(_) => None,
602	        }
603	    }
604	    let mut declared = TypeNames::default();
605	    oxc_ast_visit::Visit::visit_program(&mut declared, program);
606	    let mut aliases = FxHashMap::default();
607	    for statement in &program.body {
608	        let declaration = match statement {
609	            Statement::ExportDeclaration(export) => Some(&export.declaration),
610	            _ => statement.as_declaration(),
611	        };
612	        let Some(Declaration::TSTypeAliasDeclaration(declaration)) = declaration else { continue };
613	        let mut ty = &declaration.type_annotation;
614	        while let TSType::TSParenthesizedType(inner) = ty {
615	            ty = &inner.type_annotation;
616	        }
617	        let queried = match ty {
618	            TSType::TSTypeQuery(query) if declaration.type_parameters.is_none() && query.type_arguments.is_none() => {
619	                match &query.expr_name {
620	                    TSTypeQueryExprName::IdentifierReference(id) => Some(id.name.as_str().to_owned()),
621	                    TSTypeQueryExprName::QualifiedName(qualified) => {
622	                        chain(&qualified.left).map(|left| format!("{left}.{}", qualified.right.name))
623	                    }
624	                    TSTypeQueryExprName::ThisExpression(_) | TSTypeQueryExprName::TSImportType(_) => None,
625	                }
626	            }
627	            _ => None,
628	        };
629	        if let Some(queried) = queried
630	            && declared.0.get(declaration.id.name.as_str()) == Some(&1)
631	        {
632	            aliases.insert(CompactString::from(declaration.id.name.as_str()), CompactString::from(queried));
633	        }
634	    }
635	    aliases
636	}
